text: A loud humming filled the air, the windows vibrated. “Oh, Jack,” she cried, “another—” but her voice was drowned in the scream of a shell tearing through the clouds overhead. “That is the nearest yet,” she murmured. “Oh, no,” he answered cheerfully, “it probably fell way over by Montmartre,” and as she did not answer, he said again with exaggerated unconcern, “They wouldn’t take the trouble to fire at the Latin Quarter; anyway they haven’t a battery that can hurt it.” After a while she spoke up brightly: “Jack, dear, when are you going to take me to see Monsieur West’s statues?” “I will bet,” he said, throwing down his palette and walking over to the window beside her, “that Colette has been here to-day.” “Why?” she asked, opening her eyes very wide. Then, “Oh, it’s too bad!—really, men are tiresome when they think they know everything!
